content:
After two years of silence, Apple is developing a brand-new iMac with an M6 chip and updated colour options, according to Bloomberg reporter Mark Gurman. The new machine is expected to launch "before the end of the year."

The iMac's update cycle has always been infrequent — it has skipped both the M2 and M5 chip generations, and there is still no larger-screen option available. Apple instead recommends high-end users pair a Mac Studio or Mac mini with a Studio Display. Nevertheless, Apple is preparing to release a new version with the M6 chip.

Gurman revealed that this update will bring "several new colour options," but did not mention any specific changes. Apple slightly tweaked the tones in its 2024 M4 refresh, though the seven colour options actually remained the same — only the shades differed. The new iMac is also expected to launch before the end of the year.

This means autumn could be a fairly significant season for Mac. On the cards are a major MacBook Pro revamp with a touchscreen and Tandem OLED, a new entry-level 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6, new Mac Studio models with M5 Max and M5 Ultra (subject to supply), and a new iMac with M6. Another possibility is an updated Mac mini with M6 and M5 Pro, but that machine is very likely to arrive later.

Apple's M6 chip will be the first Mac chip built on the new 2nm process, though reportedly there will be no M6 Pro, M6 Max, or M6 Ultra variants — Apple will instead accelerate the rollout of the M7 series.
